baseline: Second optimization pass, source snapshot at start of third pass; see 2026-10-28-round2.jsonl.
method: Compiled ESM harness. Serialization warmup 200 ms, five samples; scaling repeats 10000 iterations. Final RPC pair: 1000 ms warmup, 2000 iterations, five samples, Node main thread CPU 2 / C++ peer main thread CPU 3. Older records without warmupMs used 200 ms.

decisions.41-scalar: Retained: checked numeric locations avoid Pointer/metadata allocation on valid near scalar access; far/error fallback preserves previous checks.
decisions.42b-list: Retained: primitive lists and Data read paths use numeric near locations.
decisions.43-pack-views: Retained: consume packed views directly in final output instead of trimming/copying each intermediate.
decisions.44-unpack-view: Retained: read bounded packed input views directly; snapshot shared input.
decisions.45-error: Retained: decode remote reason once and reuse it in MethodError.
decisions.49-copy-pointer: Temporary rollback only; optimized copyBuffer restored after isolated, profiled, order-balanced, and CPU-pinned comparisons.
decisions.62-short-text: Retained: 0-8-byte ASCII decode without a byte view; larger/non-ASCII input uses TextDecoder.
decisions.63-composite-snapshot: Reverted: small/inconsistent performance change did not justify specialized snapshot logic.

omittedRuns: 42-list: a temporary typo was being corrected and validation overlapped; use 42b-list.

allocationProbe.scope: Prepared UInt32 scalar reader, prepared composite element field, prepared UInt32List.get; values 42; setup excluded; result and traversal charges checked. Estimates include profiler/harness overhead; they are not exact per-read allocation counts or native backing-store measurements.

caveats: Both bulk-copy variants had fast and slow unpinned RPC runs; the original short-run regression was not reproduced under controlled comparison.
The exact cause of unpinned timing bimodality remains unresolved; late JIT tiering was observed, but is not proven to explain all variation.
CPU profiles include instrumentation overhead and are not benchmark timing results.
Near primitive access avoids wrapper allocation; far pointers, constructing readers, snapshots, text/BigInt results, and message setup are not allocation-free.
